items.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
items.summary_1line: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but often require many decoding rounds to complete a response. Efficient generation depends not only on which tokens are easy to predic...
items.editor_note: Proposes learning when to commit tokens, reducing the decoding rounds dLLMs need.

editorial.tldr: Diffusion language models first appeared here as the backbone of a tool-using chemistry agent. Days later they turned up on the offensive side, as a way to craft fluent black-box attacks on LLMs.
editorial.whats_new: A new paper distills a decoding schedule so diffusion LLMs commit tokens in fewer rounds, targeting the parallel-generation speedup that has been hard to realize.
editorial.why_it_matters: Diffusion LLMs only pay off for serving if parallel decoding cuts rounds without hurting quality; this is research-stage evidence, not a deployable runtime.
editorial.take_for_builders: Do not plan serving capacity around diffusion LLMs yet; if you prototype one, measure decoding rounds and quality against your autoregressive baseline, and include fluent-prompt attacks in red-team evals.

status.detail: Three arXiv papers, no production release: agents, attacks and decoding speed are each explored once.
